row.evidence: Salesforce's Spiff help documents SAML SSO with Google, Okta and Entra ID and says users are added manually, by .csv import or by syncing from a connected system such as Salesforce; no SCIM provisioning is documented.
row.notes: Spiff was acquired by Salesforce and is sold as Salesforce Spiff (spiff.com no longer resolves); single listed price $75/user/month billed annually. SAML SSO uses custom SAML apps in Google Workspace, Okta and Entra ID (no SCIM). Users come from manual entry, .csv import, or data connectors (Salesforce, third-party webhook). No SCIM found in the help docs index, the Spiff developer guide (Reporting, Import/Object, Webhook, System Activity Log Export APIs) or the pricing page, so status is none by absence. The System Activity Log Export API provides audit data. Spiff is also bundled in Agentforce Sales' top edition.

plans.name: Salesforce Spiff
plans.notes: Single listed plan; SSO via SAML documented without a plan gate.

deprovision.notes: No SCIM. Manual archiving hides the user from the Users table, search and statements and turns off data syncing (c11).

scim.notes: Not offered by absence: SCIM is not mentioned in the SSO article, the user-management articles or the developer guide.

webhooks_user_events.notes: The Spiff Webhook API is inbound (third-party data into Spiff), not outbound user events (c17).

user_api.notes: The Import API and Object API import records such as teams and team assignments and CRUD Spiff objects; whether user records can be managed through them is not stated in the guides, and the YAML references returned 403 to curl.

okta.notes: Spiff's guide creates a custom Okta SAML app; okta.com/integrations/spiff/ returned 404.

entra.notes: Custom enterprise application; learn.microsoft.com spiff-tutorial returned 404.

google.notes: Custom SAML app in Google Workspace.

fallbacks.other_sync: User records synced from connected systems (Salesforce connector, third-party connectors/webhook)
